strategies/a-19.title: A-19 Double
strategies/a-19.text:
A-19 Double
Definition
A-19 is a ratio-style option hedge:
buy 1 lot and sell 2 lots
. It is intended for low-to-moderate VIX, rangebound or resistance-area markets where sold premium can decay while the bought leg protects part of the tail move.
Base Structure
Bullish CE-side example:
Leg
Action
Nearer/lower CE strike
Buy 1 lot
Higher CE strike
Sell 2 lots
Optional far OTM weekly CE
Buy 1 lot for margin/tail protection
PE side is possible but needs more adjustment skill. For indexes, the source prefers CE side.
Entry Conditions
VIX should be low or stable; avoid VIX above 23.
Avoid when VIX is falling from a convergence point and market can rally steadily.
Prefer rangebound market near major resistance for CE-side structures.
Do not create CE ratio near support.
Higher buy premium relative to sell premium is acceptable; defined risk is the debit.
Know the risk zone and expiry breakeven before entry.
Strike Selection
Buy around a meaningful strike based on the view.
Sell strike can be approximated by
buy strike + buy premium
, rounded to nearest strike.
Example: buy 16000 CE at 229.95, sell two 16300 CE around 109.55.
Optional weekly far OTM buy reduces margin and helps with large overnight gaps.
Profit Logic
Downside: loss should be limited to debit if no additional shorts are added.
Rangebound: sold premium decay is the main profit engine.
Moderate upside: bought leg gains and sold legs decay/offset.
Strong upside beyond breakeven: loss can begin; adjustment required.
Adjustment Rules
Periodically book profit from the sell side.
If market falls, sell additional far OTM calls above the buying strike; never sell below the buying strike.
If market jumps sharply to a new zone, exit both legs and rebuild near the new level.
If upside band blast occurs, exit ratio and convert to bull call spread.
Keep margin reserved for adjustment.
Exit Rules
Book stock spread profit around 40-45% of maximum profit.
Far OTM stock spread may hold to 60-70% of maximum profit.
Index spread may hold to 60-70% of maximum profit.
Exit/rebuild if market reaches a new view zone quickly.
Exit if the structure violates the planned risk zone.
Backtest Specification
Minimum test inputs:
- Underlying: Nifty, Bank Nifty, or liquid stock options.
- Entry date/time relative to monthly expiry.
- VIX filter: exclude VIX > 23.
- Market regime filter: rangebound near resistance, or define by Bollinger/VWAP/20 SMA.
- Strikes: one bought, two sold, optional far OTM weekly buy.
- Entry price: actual option premium at signal time.
- Exit: 40%, 60%, 70% of max profit variants; expiry hold variant.
- Adjustment variants: no adjustment, book sell-side profit, rebuild on breakout.
Cross-Check vs Rita's BB Breakout V2
A-19 is not a breakout-following strategy; it is mostly range/resistance premium decay.
If BB breakout v2 confirms a strong band blast, A-19 ratio should be avoided or converted to directional spread.
A-19 can be backtested separately as an options payoff/regime strategy before mixing with BB scanner signals.

Arbitrage 2.0 (Future Arbitrage V2)
Definition
Arbitrage 2.0
is Rita's filtered F1/F2 backwardation strategy, now codified in
backtest_future_arbitaage.py
. It trades only one structure:
Spot > Current-month future > Next-month future
Action:
Buy current-month future, sell next-month future.
Profit comes from the current-month future converging toward spot before expiry.
Do Not Mix
This structure is NOT Arbitrage 2.0:
Spot > Current-month future < Next-month future
That is a separate calendar-credit setup and must be tracked separately. Arbitrage 2.0 requires both futures below spot AND current future above next future.

passes_entry_rules

100 contracts

100 contracts

Where:
-
basis = spot − curr.close
-

-

-

strategies/hedge-23.title: Hedge 23 (H-23)
strategies/hedge-23.text:
Hedge 23 (H-23)
Definition
Hedge 23
= Selling
deep ITM options
(with 70%+ chips/intrinsic value) to capture the
hawa (time value)
. The hedge gives "space" — if you're wrong, you exit cost-to-cost or with minor loss.
Core Philosophy
Buy the chips (intrinsic value), sell the hawa (time value). Deep ITM options behave like futures.
When to Execute
High VIX
→ high premium → high profit (best time)
Normal VIX
→ normal premium → less profit but still works
Never
jump in-between — execute only
near major support/resistance
Mark S/R on
weekly + daily charts
using BB (upper band = resistance, lower band = support)
Three Types of Risk (NK's Framework)
Known Risk
— you know your risk & reward upfront
Unknown Risk
— trade taken blindly (tips, TV news) — avoid
Planned Risk
— risk planned before entry → minimized via hedging
Planned Risk = Hedge = Insurance
Design — With Future (Positional)
Bullish View
Mark major support (e.g., Bank Nifty near 35000)
Buy
Bank Nifty MAY FUT @ 37365
Sell
Bank Nifty MAY 35000 CE @ 2890 (deep ITM, near support)
Chips-Hawa Calculation:
- Chips = Future Price − Strike = 37365 − 35000 =
2365
- Hawa = Premium − Chips = 2890 − 2365 =
525
-
Target:
Capture the 525 points of hawa
Bearish View
Mark major resistance (e.g., Bank Nifty near 39000)
Sell
Bank Nifty MAY FUT @ 37365
Sell
Bank Nifty MAY 39000 PE @ 2319 (deep ITM, near resistance)
Chips-Hawa Calculation:
- Chips = Strike − Future Price = 39000 − 37365 =
1135
- Hawa = Premium − Chips = 2319 − 1135 =
684
(approx)
-
Note:
In bearish view, you SELL BOTH future AND option
Design — With Options (Intraday)
Best Times for Pure-Chips Options
Wednesday after 2:30 PM:
Can get ITM with no hawa, 300-400 points below spot
Expiry day (Thursday) ~11 AM:
Can get ITM with no hawa, 100-200 points below spot
Example
Buy
BNF 7th APR 36700 CE @ 322 (acts as future, full chips)
Sell
BNF MAY 35000 CE @ 2890
Market up → delta difference profit
Market crashes 600-700 points → weekly CE loses only premium, MAY CE rewards 600-700 points
Adjustment (If Trade Goes Against You)
Bullish Trade Reversal
Original: Buy MAY FUT + Sell MAY 35000 CE
Adjustment:
Sell current month CE
at resistance strike
Example: Sell BNF APR 37000 CE @ 1060
SL = Strike + Premium = 37000 + 1060 = 38060
If market crosses 38060 → SL hit on adjustment CE
Advantages of Hedge 23
Very reliable hedge
Exits cost-to-cost or minor loss even if wrong
ITM options behave like futures
Works in intraday AND positional
Can be done with futures OR weekly options
Important Rules
Always build at
next month expiry
(more time, more hawa to capture)
CE side is easier to adjust than PE side —
prefer CE for bullish
Start with
positional first
, then try intraday
Start with
Index first
, then stock options
Only enemy =
VIX
(sudden VIX rise adds premium to short position)
Mark support/resistance on
weekly chart
with BB before entry
Keep adjustment area and entry area clearly defined
Chips-Hawa Formula Summary
Chips (Call) = Future Price − Strike
Chips (Put) = Strike − Future Price
Hawa = Option Premium − Chips
Target = Capture the Hawa

strategies/nifty-daily-theta.text:
Nifty Daily Theta — Sell Premium Every Day with Hedge
Core Philosophy
Sell a little theta every single day. Not once a week — EVERY DAY.
Small ₹8-15 credit, hedged with a protective long leg, repeat 200+ times a year. The grind builds the fund steadily. No single day can drain the account because every trade is a defined-risk spread.
What This Is
A
daily credit spread
on Nifty that fires Mon-Wed (skip Thu/Fri). Each trade sells a far-OTM option and buys an even further-OTM hedge. Maximum loss is the spread width minus the credit —
known at entry, capped, no unlimited risk.
This is NOT:
- ❌ Naked selling (unlimited risk)

Stock Premium Mill — Monthly Hedged Covered Calls & Puts
Core Philosophy
Same mill concept, different grindstone.
Stocks don't have weekly expiry, so we collect premium MONTHLY using covered calls on shares you own, or cash-secured puts on stocks you want to own. Slower than Nifty, but you build an equity portfolio while collecting premium.
What This Strategy Is
A
monthly stock option selling system
that generates premium income from stocks you already hold (or want to hold). Two modes:
Covered Call mode:
You own 1000 shares of SBIN → sell monthly OTM call against them → collect premium. If called away, you sell at a profit. If not, you keep shares + premium.
Cash-Secured Put mode:
You want to buy Tata Motors at ₹900 (currently ₹950) → sell ₹900 put → collect ₹15 premium. If assigned, you buy at ₹885 (₹900 - ₹15). If not, keep premium.
This is NOT:
- ❌ Naked option selling on random stocks
- ❌ Day trading options
- ❌ Buying options (you're the casino, not the gambler)
This IS:
- ✅ Selling time value on stocks you understand
- ✅ Monthly income from portfolio holdings
- ✅ Getting paid to wait for entry prices (put selling)
- ✅ Getting paid to exit at profit targets (call selling)

concepts/arbitrage.text:
Concept: Arbitrage (Futures-Spot Gap Trading)
Definition
Arbitrage in equity markets means exploiting price gaps between two related instruments — typically the
futures price
and the
spot (cash) price
of the same stock or index. The trade profits when the gap narrows or closes.
How It Works (in Indian Markets)
Leg
Action
Futures overpriced vs spot
Sell futures, buy spot
Futures underpriced vs spot (backwardation)
Buy futures, sell spot (or sell F2, buy F1)
Rita's
Future Arbitrage strategy
is a specific type: F1/F2 spread in backwardation (F1 < spot, F2 < F1).
Key Properties
Limited risk
: Maximum loss is bounded (unlike naked futures)
Rollover available
: If trade goes wrong, you can roll the position to the next expiry — no forced unlimited loss
Time-based
: Gap tends to close as expiry approaches (convergence)
Requires patience
: Entry timing is critical — wrong entry = unnecessary loss even if direction is right
Rules/Thresholds from Sources
Monitor
historical gap sizes
before trading — trade only gaps that are statistically significant
Never exceed
capital capacity
— position sizing discipline is non-negotiable
Wait for
correct entry point
— impulsive entry is the #1 cause of avoidable loss
Types of Arbitrage (mentioned in source, not detailed)
Futures-Spot arbitrage
F1-F2 spread (inter-expiry)
Others not specified in this source
Risks
Gap can widen before closing (short-term drawdown)
Rollover has a cost (spread, brokerage)
Requires monitoring of external factors: crude oil, currency (INR/USD)

concepts/atr.title: ATR (Average True Range)
concepts/atr.text:
ATR (Average True Range)
Definition
ATR
measures the
average price movement range
per candle over a specified period. It quantifies volatility — not direction.
Formula
ATR = average of True Range over N periods, where:
- True Range = max(High−Low, |High−PrevClose|, |Low−PrevClose|)
NK Usage
Mentioned in
convergence of moving averages
context
Used to measure
thickness of S/R zones
Helps determine
stop-loss width
— wider stops needed when ATR is high
Helps gauge whether a stock is
scalp-friendly
(low ATR) or
volatile
(high ATR)
Practical Applications
ATR Level
Implication
High ATR
Volatile stock — wider S/R, wider stops, bigger moves
Low ATR
Calm stock — tighter S/R, scalp-friendly, smaller moves
ATR expanding
Breakout/volatility incoming
ATR contracting
Consolidation — potential BB squeeze forming
Relationship to Other Indicators
Bollinger Bands:
BB width correlates with ATR (BB = 20 SMA ± 2×std dev)
S/R zones:
Higher ATR → wider effective S/R bands
Position sizing:
Use ATR to normalize risk across different stocks
Stop placement:
SL = entry − (multiple × ATR) for volatility-adjusted stops
Note
ATR is
secondary
in NK's system — primarily used as a
risk management aid
, not a primary signal generator. The primary signals come from HM, VWAP, BB, and COMA.

concepts/bb-blast.text:
BB Blast (Bollinger Band Breakout)
Definition
A
continuation/breakout
event: after a period of band
squeeze
(low volatility, narrow bands), price blasts out of a band and rides it — the start of a trending move. This is the NK pattern most analogous to what Rita's
BB breakout v2
scanner hunts.
Confirmation rules (from
Source Class 6 Ohol
)
A BB Blast is confirmed when
all four
hold:
1.
Band squeeze
came first (narrow bands / momentum compressed).
2.
Movement on higher TF
— momentum sustains on the higher timeframe.
3.
Movement on lower TF
— momentum sustains on the lower timeframe.
4. (Implied) blast direction = the side it exits.
If bands were
not
narrow and price still blasts → it's a
BB Trap
, not a real blast.
Expected duration by timeframe (the key table)
Timeframe
Expected effect duration
10 min
1.5 – 2 hours

5 – 15 days

Intraday (15-min,
Source Ma Convergence

buy only above 20 SMA (the middle band), sell only below; confirm with
Vwap

Hilega Milega

on a BB Blast,
buy OTM, sell further OTM

when price closes back inside the band / below 20 SMA.

concepts/bb-trap.title: BB Trap (Bollinger Band Trap)
concepts/bb-trap.text:
BB Trap (Bollinger Band Trap)
Definition
A
reversal
pattern where retailers get trapped on a fake gap move. Price gaps up/down, the first candle closes
outside
the Bollinger Band, the next candle
re-enters and closes below VWAP
— the move fails and reverses hard. "Because this traps the retailers, it's called BB Trap." It is the
opposite
of
BB Blast
(which
sustains
outside the band; the trap
fails
to sustain).
Why it works
Market gaps → retailers pile in at the open.
Smart money sells into that buying at the high.
Price collapses back below VWAP and stays there all day → retailers trapped.
"Where retailers get trapped, only there you make money."
Identification rules (from
Source Bb Trap Mentorship3
)
Use
15-min / 30-min / 1-hour
TF.
Look only at scripts with a
strong gap up/down open
.
Minimum one candle must close outside the band.
Next candle comes back inside the band
AND closes below the low of the outside-band candle.
Following candles stay
below VWAP
and sustain.
→ Short (after confirmation) near VWAP. For options, take
ATM
.
BB Trap on 15-min (Bank Nifty example,
Source Bb Trap Hedging
)
500-pt gap up; entire first candle outside upper band.
Next candle closes below prior candle AND below VWAP.
SL above the high of the prior (outside-band) candle.
Variants / intensity
Frequency:
forms
5–6 times/month in indices, 2–3 times/month in a stock.
Bigger TF = bigger money.
Jackpot trade:
BB Trap on
all three TFs
simultaneously (15/30/60 min) → very big move. Occurs
once in 2–3 months.
"Very little SL hunting in this pattern."
Positional BB Trap:
use on
daily TF
. On
monthly chart
→ signals a massive fall.
The 4 ways to trade a BB Trap (from
Source Bb Trap Hedging
, Indigo example)
Choose based on
capital, risk tolerance, and emotion
:
#
Trade
Notes
1
Cash intraday (MIS)
Sell short in cash; MIS only, never NRML/carry
2
Short Future + hedge
Sell Future + sell ATM Put simultaneously (premium income + directional)
3
Sell Call above VWAP
Naked or hedged; hedge = buy a call 50 pts above the sold strike. Hedged profit smaller (~8–9 pts) but no system SL needed
4
Buy 1-strike-away OTM Put + sell far OTM Put
Defined risk = buy−sell premium; e.g. risk ₹19 for the full month
Worked hedge math (Indigo, BB Trap short)
Entry 1672 (below the VWAP-close candle).
Future + Put hedge:
short Indigo future + short 1600 PE @67.95 → put MTM loss ₹15.05, future +46 → net
+31 pts
.
Call spread:
short 1680 CE (high 63.90) + buy 1730 CE (hedge) → capped risk, smaller profit.
Put spread:
buy 1660 PE @67 + sell 1620 PE @48 → max risk
₹19
for the month.
Stop-loss
System SL:
above the high of the outside-band candle.
Practical SL:
wait for a
full candle to close above VWAP
before quitting.
If hedged:
no system SL needed.
When NOT to trade a BB Trap
Lower-band BB Trap + Open = High
→ avoid.
Upper-band BB Trap + Open = Low
→ avoid.
Supreme override
"
BB Trap and 3-step is supreme.
" If BB Trap +
three-step pattern
forms,
ignore Hilega-Milega signals.
Retailer trapping does not show on indicators until later.
How to hedge a Future in a BB Trap (Bank Nifty,
Source Bb Trap Hedging
)
Short Nifty future + buy ITM Call with
~70% chips
(≈300 pts ITM) → risk per lot ≈
10 pts
, margin ≈ ₹34,000/lot. No system SL needed when hedged.
Or: short Future + short ATM Put (high VIX → sell put; low VIX → buy call).
Cross-check vs Rita's BB breakout v2
BB Trap is a
reversal
; BB breakout v2 is a
continuation
. They are distinct patterns but share the BB + VWAP vocabulary. When v2 is documented, confirm v2 explicitly
excludes
trap setups (i.e. requires the breakout to sustain, not re-enter the band) — this is exactly the trap-vs-blast distinction NK draws.

concepts/bollinger-bands.title: Bollinger Bands
concepts/bollinger-bands.text:
Bollinger Bands
Definition
A
volatility indicator
(John Bollinger): a band plotted at
±2 standard deviations
around a
20-period SMA
(defaults: period 20, stddev 2). Upper band = resistance, lower band = support, middle = 20 SMA. The band width expands/contracts with volatility.
Core behaviours (NK framework)
Squeeze → blast:
when bands are narrow for a while (low volatility), a sharp directional move becomes likely. If bands were
not
narrow and it "blasts" → likely a
trap
.
Band walk:
a strong trend can "walk" along a band — stay in the trade till price leaves the band.
Mean reversion inside range:
price tends to bounce between bands; bounce off lower band + cross above middle → upper band is the target.
Breakout invalidation:
if price exits a band but immediately re-enters → the breakout strength is negated.
Timeframe effect (from
Source Class 6 Ohol
):
a BB event on day TF → 7–28 days effect; hourly → 2–3 days. (BB Blast duration table on
Bb Blast
.)
Confirmation:
BB blast + next day gap up + sustain = confirmed.
Intraday trading rules (15-min, from
Source Ma Convergence
)
Buy only when candle is
above the 20 SMA
(black/middle line).
Sell only when candle is
below 20 SMA
.
Confirm with
Vwap
+
Hilega Milega
.
"Whenever it touches 20 SMA, price will jump."
Two NK signature BB patterns
BB Blast
— the continuation/breakout (and the pattern your BB breakout v2 scanner targets).
BB Trap
— the reversal trap (retailers get caught on a fake gap move).
BB in the broader method
Combined with
Vwap
(the "station"),
Avwap
,
Hilega Milega
(confirmation), and the 20/50/100/150/200 EMA
COMA
stack.
Moh Maya
uses BB as its outside-the-band trigger.
Overbought Oversold
is partly read via BB.
AVWAP "works well with Bollinger Band also."

This is the critical gap flagged in

.
Rita is building a Bollinger Band breakout scanner for Nifty 500 stocks; the scanner logic (call it "BB breakout v2") is
not documented anywhere in the vault.
Per the schema's hard rule, I should cross-check every BB source against it — but there's nothing to check against yet.
What the sources say BB-breakout-like behaviour looks like
(for comparison once v2 is documented):
- Squeeze then blast, ride the band (
Source Ma Convergence
)
- Buy above 20 SMA on 15-min; exit when price closes below 20 SMA
- Confirm with VWAP + HM
- BB Blast duration-by-TF table (
Source Class 6 Ohol
): 10-min → 1.5–2 hr, 30-min → 2–5 days, day → 5–15 days, weekly → 20–25 days, monthly → 3–7 months.
Claimed 70% accuracy
(unvalidated).
- On BB Blast: buy OTM, sell further OTM (
Source Option Calculation
)
- Moh-Maya: outside-band doji → next-day entry (positional variant)
- Warning: a "blast"
without
prior narrowing is a trap

Chips & Hawa (Intrinsic vs Time Value)
Definition
NK's house vocabulary for option pricing:
-
Chips
=
Intrinsic Value
— the real, "yours to keep" portion.
-
Hawa
=
Time Value
(literally "air") — the speculative portion that decays to zero by expiry.
"Chips are yours, hawa is a dream."
Formulas
For a Call: Chips = Spot − Strike
For a Put: Chips = Strike − Spot
For both: Hawa = Premium − Chips
⚠️
Nuance:
chips/hawa are
defined
using
spot price
, but the option's
behaviour
follows the
future price
. (
Options
)
Fast mental calc (rule of thumb)
Spot − nearest ATM gives the rough "chips width" per 100 points. E.g. spot 14507, ATM 14500 → 14500−14200 = 300 → a 14200 CE has ~300 chips. ~90–100% accuracy.
Moneyness → chips/hawa split
Type
Chips
Hawa
Far ITM
mostly chips
little
Near ITM
chips + hawa
some
ATM
≈ 0

The NK house rules (the whole point)
Buyers buy chips (ITM), never OTM.
ITM behaves like the future — minimal time decay. OTM is pure hawa that dissolves.
Sellers sell hawa (OTM), never ITM.
You collect the hawa as profit; it goes to zero on expiry.
Hedge pattern:
buy ITM (pay chips+hawa) + sell far OTM (collect 100% hawa) → effective cost drops, breakeven shifts favorably. Worked examples in
Source Option Basics

BB Blast

concepts/discipline-and-emotions.title: Concept: Discipline & Emotions in Trading
concepts/discipline-and-emotions.text:
Concept: Discipline & Emotions in Trading
Definition
The ability to follow your trading rules consistently, even when fear (of loss) or greed (of more profit) create pressure to deviate.
Why It Matters
Traders with solid technical knowledge still lose consistently because emotional reactions override their rules. This is the most common gap between knowing and doing in trading.
Core Emotions to Manage
Emotion
Trigger
Typical Mistake
Fear
Position in loss, market falling
Panic exit at worst price
Greed
Position in profit, market running
Hold too long, give back gains
Impatience
Watching price move without a position
Impulsive entry at wrong point
Rules from Sources
Hold positions
— don't panic-sell during drawdown if the trade thesis is intact
Wait for entry
— patience at entry is more valuable than any indicator
Track your trades
— reviewing past trades builds pattern recognition and confidence over time
Operate within capacity
— exceeding your capital limit amplifies emotional pressure and causes irrational decisions
Develop original strategy
— copying others creates dependency and lack of conviction, making discipline harder
Relation to Rita's Strategy
Rita's BB breakout v2 manual validation process (7-point checklist before GTT placement) is a direct application of discipline — the checklist exists to prevent impulsive trades. This concept underpins why that process was designed that way.

Definition
An exit is the pre-planned rule that protects profit or limits loss. The source emphasizes that best entry is less important than a defined exit.

Long taken below/near lower area: exit near 20 SMA if that is the planned target.
Short taken above/near upper area: exit near 20 SMA if that is the planned target.
20 SMA often breaks by gap or large candle; do not assume a gentle exit.
20 SMA can also become reversal area if other rules confirm.

concepts/futures.title: Futures
concepts/futures.text:
Futures
Definition
A derivative contract that is a
right
and obligation
to buy or sell an underlying at a predetermined price, settled on a predetermined
expiry
. Unlike an option, there is no "premium decay" — both sides are obligated, and profit/loss accrues daily via MTM.
Mechanics
Expiry:
index & stock futures =
last Thursday
of the month (previous trading day if holiday).
Lot size:
futures trade only in lots (exchange-fixed); NIFTY 75, BANKNIFTY 25, FINNIFTY 40 (Jan 2021 values, subject to change); stock futures vary widely (full list in
Source Option Future Basics
).
Margin:
futures require only a
~20% margin
of notional → ~5× leverage. Same leverage amplifies losses 5×.
Contract value
≥ ₹5 lakh at introduction.
MTM (Mark to Market):
at end of each trading day,
(closing − opening) × lot size
is credited/debited. Next day's opening = prior day's close.
Must maintain margin + cover MTM debits or broker squares off.
Near/Next/Far:
three expiries available;
near month has the highest liquidity
→ trade it.
Future price vs spot
The future normally trades at a
premium
to spot (time value), but can be at a discount.
Options are priced off the future
, not the spot — this is why they're called "F&O" together.
On expiry day after 12 noon, future converges to spot.
A spot/future gap of ~200 pts is itself tradeable — see
Expiry Gap Hedge
.
How NK uses futures
As the directional leg in a
Future Hedge
: buy Future + buy ITM Put (or sell Future + buy ITM Call) for limited-loss, unlimited-profit with reduced margin.
Hedge 17 uses Nifty/BankNifty
correlation
via futures + options.
The future gives the directional conviction; the option caps the risk.
Worked hedge math (from
Source Option Calculation
, Bharti Airtel)
Buy Future + buy 570 PE (chips 34, hawa 8) + sell 580 CE @7.10 → max risk ≈ ₹1.
Adjustment if price falls: roll down to 530 PE / 550 CE; sell an extra call for extra profit.

concepts/hedging.title: Hedging
concepts/hedging.text:
Hedging
Definition
A technique to ensure a market position is
not wiped out by an adverse move
— construct a portfolio (futures + options, or options + options) so that one leg's loss is offset by another's gain. NK's metaphor:
"erecting a fence around your farm."
More importantly: a
thought process
that flexes with the market.
Why hedge (the structural reason)
Margin reduction:
a hedged combo needs far less margin than naked legs. E.g. SBI Jan future alone = ₹3,02,591; the matching put alone = ₹54,450;
combined-hedged = ₹84,611
(≈ intraday margin) — "like magic."
Risk capping:
you can compute max loss
before
entry.
Survival:
"First loss is always the smallest." Hedging lets you make the right decision when a trade goes wrong instead of panicking.
Market-participant framing (NK's worldview)
Speculators (~4%) — Rakesh Jhunjhunwala / Buffett types
Hedgers (~5%) — FIIs, DIIs, smart money ← who actually makes money
Arbitrageurs (~92%) — common investors, who
lose
to the hedgers
Three types of risk (from
Source Hedge 23
/ Hedge 23 class)
Known risk
— you know your risk and reward upfront.
Unknown risk
— trade taken without study (tips, TV, news); you don't know what can happen.
Planned risk
— risk you
plan before entry
, then minimize/break-even/zero it after entry.
Plan Risk = Hedge = Insurance.
Do hedgers win 100% of the time? No — but the math favors them.
The universal hedge pattern (chips/hawa view)
Buy
chips
(ITM) for directional exposure → sell hawa (far OTM) to discount the purchase → net cost drops, breakeven shifts favorably, max loss is bounded. See worked examples in
Source Option Basics
and
Source Option Calculation
.
Adjustment (the discipline)
Hedges are
not set-and-forget
: roll legs as price moves (e.g. Airtel future hedge: roll 570 PE → 530 PE, 580 CE → 550 CE on a fall; sell an extra call for extra profit in a downtrend). Book the long leg when it reaches 95% price + 5% chips, or when its liquidity dries up.
When NOT to hedge / when to exit
If trend reverses against a multi-leg position and it looks like a
trap
→ exit
all
positions and rebuild for the new conditions (
Source Option Calculation
).
"First loss is always the smallest" — don't widen the timeframe to avoid booking it.
Named hedge strategies in this wiki
Hedge 23
— the flagship, VIX-aware
Hedge 17
— Nifty/BankNifty correlation, monthly+weekly
Future Hedge
— Future + ITM Put/Call
Wednesday Hedge
— weekly OTM strangle
Expiry Gap Hedge
— spot/future gap arbitrage
A 19
— A19 double, 1-lot-long/2-lot-short

concepts/hilega-milega.title: Hilega Milega (HM)
concepts/hilega-milega.text:
Hilega Milega (HM)
Definition
NK's proprietary composite indicator built on
RSI(9)
with three overlays:
-
21-period Weighted MA
on RSI → the
red line
(Volume)
-
3-period Weighted MA
on RSI → the
green line
(Price)
-
RSI(9) itself
(set to OB=50, OS=50 instead of default 14/70/30) → the
black line
(Strength)
- Plus
VWAP
on the price chart.
"If it dips, it delivers"
(Hilega-Milega) — the name reflects its trend-reversal signalling nature.
Primary purpose (refined Jul 2026 —
Source Nk Hm Podcast 2026
):
HM's job is
conviction / direction
, not entry timing. It tells a beginner which side to buy and which side to sell. Entry/exit still come from your own skill + price structure (VWAP, MA). It is deliberately simple so newcomers see clear direction instead of "everything looks green/red."
How to set up (Zerodha Kite)
Add RSI → set period to
9
, Overbought=50, Oversold=50
Add Weighted MA → period
21
, field = RSI(9) → red line
Add Weighted MA → period
3
, field = RSI(9) → green line
Add VWAP on price chart
Setup refinements (Jul 2026 podcast)
Why RSI(9), not 14:
RSI(14) lags; 9 reacts before the crowd (which all use 14). NK tested 2/3/5/7/10/14 and settled on 9/10.
Conditional RSI(7):
when the market is heavily down OR
SRT
≤ ~0.85, shift HM to period
7
for faster response.
The red line is a volume proxy, not real volume.
WMA was chosen (over all 11 MA types) because it tracks volume averages closest. Critical on Nifty/index futures where volume is unreliable. Many users wrongly assume it is real volume — see
Nk Volume Reading
.
Planned migration to VMA:
NK is researching shifting the overlay to Variable Moving Average (market structure changed post-2022). 1–2 years out; HM still works.
Broker caveat:
many brokers don't allow an indicator-on-indicator overlay — a practical setup problem.
Reading the signals
Signal
Meaning
Red below Black and Blue
BUY zone
Red above Green and Black
SELL zone
Green above Black
SELL
Below water (Blue / RSI below 50)
SELL
Red line below Black → price stops going down
Selling exhaustion
Gap between Green and Black
Market won't go up
Red line crosses below Black line
Stop selling, start buying
Black 20 SMA turns upward + candle above
Stop selling
Trading rules refined (Jul 2026 podcast)
Stay buy-biased while red (WMA) line stays below the RSI line
— ignore even a textbook price breakdown (close below prior low) if the red line is still under RSI. Price can "do whatever drama."
Sell/exit trigger:
red line crosses
above
RSI and sustains (esp. with divergence forming) → expect a fall → book profit on your TF.
RSI 86 = universal profit-booking level.
Any timeframe — when RSI hits 86, book and exit. After 86, RSI won't immediately re-hit; expect pullback/consolidation, then trend resumes.
Swing survival through the post-86 pullback:
ride
SMA 100 on 1-hour TF
(or 50/63) — it protects and marks re-entry.
RSI 55 false-signal filter:
raise the mid-line from 50 to 55; only buy when the HM curve completes a
V-shape
AND RSI > 55.
Old-low-break stat:
when HM flips to buy then immediately flips back to sell, the prior swing low breaks "very badly/fast" — backtested ~10 times,
works 8/10
.
Timeframe hierarchy
Positional:
analyze on Day/Week/Month, execute on 1-hr/Day
Intraday:
analyze on 1-hr/Day, execute on 15-min/30-min
Swing:
use ≥
3-hour TF
(going below 3h needs expertise; beginners in range-bound markets on small TFs get hurt and wrongly conclude "HM doesn't work").
Don't try to catch bottoms/tops.
20 SMA = best support/resistance; use hourly for entry/exit. On smaller/intraday TFs use
VMA (Variable Moving Average)
instead of fixed SMA — it adapts to price.
Larger TF = higher accuracy.
Below 5m/10m needs deep understanding or HM "won't work" (10-ft ladder against a 5-story building).
Does NOT work in range-bound markets
— and no momentum indicator does. Not a flaw; a scope limit.
Critical role in the NK method
HM is the
confirmation filter
— used alongside
Vwap
,
Bollinger Bands
,
Avwap
, and
COMA
for every major ent

concepts/htl-rotation.title: Concept: HTL Rotation (Gold ↔ Nifty Fund-Flow Switch)
concepts/htl-rotation.text:
Definition
HTL Rotation
is the regime switch popularized by the HT Legend 6-year ledger video: when money flows
out of Nifty/equities into gold
, shift the option-writing book from index premium to
gold premium
(and back when the flow reverses). It is a two-asset specialization of
regime mapping
— instead of adjusting strategy parameters per regime, you
change the underlying you sell premium on
, keeping the theta-decay engine constant while the market decides which asset pays.
Named so the vault has one handle for the idea.
Mechanics are the source's claim, not our validation
— see HTL Thread for the running comparison.
Claimed mechanics (per the source — unverified)
A green/red
fund-flow dial
between gold and Nifty: green = money rotating into gold from other asset classes → trade gold; flow back into Nifty → trade index.
Claimed gold era:
~Oct 2024 – Apr 2026
; claimed distribution signal: Nifty rose 24k → ~25k in early 2025
while
funds flowed out.
Entries
near candle lows
(pullback entries within a flow-confirmed direction), hedged option writing, most positions covered before expiry, profit mostly theta.
Claimed output: ~₹1.06 Cr on gold in ~18 months, "8–9%/month" on deployed capital.
Why it matters to us
Convergent independent witness:
NK's
srt investing
routes to gold independently —
weekly SRT > 1.24 → exit equities → gold / dividend / cash
. Two unconnected teachers point at the same equity-extreme → gold rotation.
Matches our own tape:
Sep-2026 paper window — NIFTY grinding down, O=H shorts winning / O=L longs bleeding, gold at highs. The rotation direction is what our live book has been screaming.
Already have the plumbing:
the goldcrypto paper engine trades GC=F daily; our validated edges (Open=Low intraday PF 4.25, BB Trap v2 shorts PF 2.10) can be re-run
gated
by this switch to measure the lift, if any.
Testable proxy (backtest candidate #0 in
regime mapping
)
Flow dial proxy:
gold/Nifty relative strength
— e.g., 50-day slope or 12/26-week RS of GC=F (or MCX gold in INR) vs NIFTY 50.
Question to answer: does gating our Nifty premium engines OFF and gold premium ON during "funds-out-of-Nifty" windows improve aggregate PF vs ungated?
Cheap first cut: classify the last ~3 years into gold-era / nifty-era windows by RS, overlay our existing backtest month-P&Ls, compare.
Hard caveats
The exact fund-flow formula was
never disclosed
— any proxy we test is ours, not theirs.
The 8–9%/month gold claim is unaudited marketing; only the
rotation direction
is being adopted for testing, nothing else.
Gold in INR has a currency component (USD/INR) a Nifty-only habit tends to forget — factor it in any backtest.
Related Concepts
regime mapping
— the parent discipline (strategy follows regime)
srt investing
— independent convergence: SRT > 1.24 → gold
hedging
/
options
— the premium-selling engine being rotated
survivorship bias
— why the source's numbers stay "claims"

— origin (2026-08-06 video)

concepts/intraday-process.title: Intraday Process
concepts/intraday-process.text:
Intraday Process
Definition
The intraday process is the wiki's top-down decision flow for daily trading: read market direction first, pick aligned stocks, wait for VWAP/20 SMA location, confirm with HM/BB, then manage exits on 10-minute candles.
Pre-Trade Filter
Avoid first 2 hours; preferred trading starts after 12:15 PM.
Check Nifty, Bank Nifty, Sensex direction.
Skip unclear direction.
Classify market as rangebound or trending.
Use top gainers in bullish market and top losers in bearish market.
Check advance/decline.
Required Chart Setup
HM system.
Bollinger Bands with 20 SMA.
VWAP.
9 SMA high.
30-minute chart for setup observation.
10-minute chart for ride/exit.
Long Setup
BB blast upside or wide-open BB with price behavior supporting trend.
Price breaks VWAP, comes near 20 SMA, bounces, and closes above VWAP.
HM buy.
RSI above 60.
Entry near 20 SMA / just above VWAP.
SL: two 10-minute closes below 20 SMA.
Trail/ride above 9 SMA high.
Short Setup
Mirror setup.
HM sell.
RSI below 45.
Entry near 20 SMA / just below VWAP.
SL: two 10-minute closes above 20 SMA.
Trail/ride below 9 SMA high.
OH-OL / BB Trap Branch
Open=High + top loser supports bearish trade.
Open=Low + top gainer supports bullish trade.
Gap-down BB Trap: only bullish side after VWAP reclaim.
Gap-up BB Trap: only bearish side after VWAP loss.
No OH/OL: use 15-minute ORB, then enter near VWAP.
Backtest Specification
Start with cash/futures signal first, then options overlay later.
Use 30-minute setup and 10-minute exit.
Test after-12:15 filter versus all-day variant.
Track index alignment, top gainer/loser rank, HM/RSI condition, VWAP/20 SMA proximity.

Source How To Do Intraday

concepts/k-wave.title: K Wave
concepts/k-wave.text:
K Wave
Definition
K Wave is a 10-minute intraday pattern where 4-5 narrow candles form after a gap near the Bollinger Band/VWAP area. A range break then leads to a strong directional move.
Setup
Timeframe: 10 minutes.
Usually forms after gap up near band area below VWAP for bearish version.
Candles are often doji/spinning tops with high wicks and no clear trend.
Entry at fifth candle or on closing break of the range.
If first entry is missed, price may return near VWAP for another entry.
SL: close above VWAP for bearish setup.
Buy-side version forms after gap down.
Priority Rule
The source says pattern should get priority over HM signal when the pattern is clear.
Backtest Specification
Detect 4-5 candles with compressed range near VWAP after gap.
Require range break close.
Exit: VWAP reclaim, fixed R multiple, EOD, or target based on move size.
Related
Source Class Notes 08 May 2022
Vwap
Bollinger Bands

concepts/killer-wave.title: Killer Wave
concepts/killer-wave.text:
Killer Wave
Definition
Killer Wave is a 1-hour intraday price-action pattern that usually appears after a gap and signals a sharp fourth/fifth-candle move. It is traded with options buying, option selling, futures, or cash depending on instrument and risk.
Bearish Setup
Use 1-hour chart.
Price gaps up or down; bearish version most often follows gap up.
First candles close below VWAP or lose VWAP quickly.
Small candles, spinning top, or inverted hammer form near VWAP / 20 SMA / upper BB zone.
VWAP slopes down or near 45-degree angle.
Entry around third or fourth candle near VWAP.
Big move expected on fourth or fifth candle.
Bullish Setup
Mirror setup: after gap down, candles close above VWAP and hold near VWAP/20 SMA before sharp upside.
Entry And Exit
Entry: third or fourth 1-hour candle near VWAP.
Conservative timing mentioned: around 12:15.
SL: one 1-hour candle close above VWAP for bearish setup; system SL above swing high / previous two candle high.
Option target: double/triple; book about 60% on double and ride 40%.
Backtest Specification
Universe: Nifty, Bank Nifty, liquid F&O stocks.
Timeframe: 1-hour candles.
Required fields: gap %, VWAP, BB 20/2, candle body/wick, option premium if testing options.
Signal: gap + first two closes below/above VWAP + small candle near VWAP.
Exit variants: fourth/fifth candle close, VWAP reclaim, option double, EOD.
Cross-Check vs BB Breakout V2
Killer Wave can contradict naive breakout buying if price gaps up but fails VWAP.
BB breakout v2 should treat VWAP loss and small candles after gap as a failure/reversal filter.

concepts/moh-maya.title: Moh Maya Pattern
concepts/moh-maya.text:
Moh Maya Pattern
Definition
Moh Maya
is a bullish reversal candlestick pattern where:
1. A candle forms
outside the lower Bollinger Band
(price closes below lower BB)
2. Next day, price
trades above VWAP
on hourly timeframe → buy signal
Name Meaning
"Moh Maya" = illusion/delusion — the breakdown below lower BB is an
illusion
; it's actually a buying opportunity.
Trading Rules
Entry
Wait for candle to form
outside lower BB
Next day, check if price trades above VWAP on
hourly chart
For safety: take trade around
3:20–3:25 PM
when price is above VWAP AND above
last day's high
Buy
monthly expiry CE option
around ₹70–80 premium
Targets & Exits
Book
half quantity
when option doubles
Or book half near
20 SMA
or create spread
Alternative: trail with SL adjustments
Stop Loss
SL =
close below lower Bollinger Band
If price violates the lower BB again after entry → exit
BB Context for Moh Maya
Band should be
thick
(high volatility) for faster upward move
5 SMA (close) is good for trading:
below 5 SMA don't buy, above 5 SMA don't sell
Price comes near 20 SMA → take trade after close above 5 SMA
Relationship to Other Concepts
Moh Maya is the
bullish opposite
of BB Trap
Moh Maya = candle below lower BB → reversal UP
BB Trap = candle above upper BB → reversal DOWN
Both patterns exploit the fact that
extreme BB penetrations are often traps

Moving Averages (MA)
Definition
A moving average smooths price data by creating a constantly updated average price over a specific period. Used for trend identification, support/resistance, and entry/exit signals.

big candle in fast manner

MAs tell you
direction

concepts/nk-volume-reading.title: NK's Volume Reading (50/50 thesis)
concepts/nk-volume-reading.text:
NK's Volume Reading (50/50 thesis)
Definition
NK sir's own framing of volume as
the one footprint big money cannot fake.
His exact split:
technical analysis = 50% price action + 50% volume.
Big money (operators/FIs) can deceive you in price, indicators, and OI — but not in volume, because every real transaction leaves a real size.
This is distinct from
Vpa
(Anna Coulling's effort-vs-result framework, which NK studied as a foundation) and
Volume Mismatch
(the single-bar signal). NK's version centers on
breakout confirmation
and the
price-volume direction agreement
.
The two-candle-close law (NK's #1 rule)
Never act on a breakout/breakdown without
two candle closes
above/below the level on the timeframe you trade.
Stated as the
single biggest source of retail losses
— bigger than any strategy flaw. Breakout/breakdown levels hold the most liquidity, which is exactly where big money distributes to retail. NK admits he lost money on the Nifty ATH breakout (26,061, Sep 2024 broken Nov–Dec 2025) by skipping this.
Breakout volume rules
Breakout volume must be
substantially higher than the surrounding 10–15–20 candles
AND in a
rising state
. No fixed multiplier — "kaafi zyada."
For
lifetime-high / 52-week-high
breakouts: if not visible on daily, check
weekly
; if not weekly, check
monthly
. On at least one TF the volume must clearly exceed the surrounding average.
Volume + candle size must match.
Huge volume + tiny candle body = red flag — question the move. "Where the volume is, the price should also be there."
The bike analogy (price-volume agreement)
Volume = handlebar. Price = bike.
Turn the handlebar left, the bike must turn left.
Volume one direction, price the other (or price stalls/freezes) =
deception
by big money. A trap.
This is the same principle as
Vpa
(effort vs result) and
Volume Mismatch
, restated as a directional-consistency check.
Big-money mechanics (why volume needs time)
Big money buys cheap in the "warehouse" (accumulation), then sells slowly to retail at the "stall" (distribution) — never all at once. This is why:
- Volume needs
time/confirmation
(the two-close rule).
- Breakout points are distribution traps, not free money.
How volume fits with Hilega Milega
Hilega Milega
gives direction/conviction;
volume is the confirmation layer on top
, not a replacement.
Do NOT jump on every minor HM signal in a sideways/range market — wait for the full HM curve + V-shape + volume confirmation.
NK's plan (in progress, not yet released): integrate real-time volume layers —
volume smash, stopping volume, sign volume
— with HM + ORB.
What NK de-emphasizes
No indicator (lagging or leading) tells you an old low will break
— HM + volume does. Indicators "cheat/deceive"; volume doesn't.
OI / PCR overrated.
Better to look at
OI percentile
(e.g. 90th percentile = price has been here only 10% of time → expect mean reversion). Nobody talks about percentile.
FII/DII cash data + IPO data are useful but underused
vs the hype around OI.
Closed-market hindsight is misleading — "anyone can show buy here/sell here after the fact."
Used in strategies
Confirmation filter for
Hilega Milega
entries
Breakout validation (links to
Bb Breakout V2
,
Bb Trap Positional
)
Reinforces
Vpa
and
Volume Mismatch
Status
⚠️
Not backtested.
NK's teaching from a podcast (auto-generated Hindi transcript, translated). The two-close law and 10–15–20-candle volume rule are specific and testable — good scanner candidates once validated. No fixed volume multiplier given.
Source
Source Nk Hm Podcast 2026
(51:10 onward — "How to read volume like a professional")

concepts/oh-ol.title: OH-OL (Open High / Open Low)
concepts/oh-ol.text:
OH-OL (Open High / Open Low)
Definition
OH-OL
is an intraday option selling strategy based on identifying stocks that make their
day's high or low in the very first candle
of the day.
OH (Open = High):
First candle high = day's high → stock unlikely to go higher →
sell CE
(deep ITM)
OL (Open = Low):
First candle low = day's low → stock unlikely to go lower →
sell PE
(deep ITM)
Core Philosophy
Treat
deep ITM options as proxy futures
— they move 1:1 with underlying
Sell
hawa (extrinsic/time value)
— the premium component above intrinsic value
Premium
decays throughout the day
→ seller profits from time decay
Keep
60% capital reserved
for adjustments if trade goes against you
Trading Process
Identify OH/OL stocks
from first candle (9:15 AM)
Check VWAP
direction — should confirm OH/OL signal
Select deep ITM strike
— high chips, low hawa
Sell the option
at or near VWAP level
Exit
when premium decays sufficiently (typically by 3:15–3:25 PM)
Key Rules
VWAP confirms the direction: above VWAP → sell PE, below VWAP → sell CE
Previous day resistance acts as resistance for next day only
Don't trade if no clear OH/OL signal in first candle
Use 1-hour chart for confirmation if not experienced

-
Total P&L:
+₹95,405

Win rate:
~77% (10/13 days profitable)

When Combined with BB + VWAP

BB Trap scenario + OH-OL = extra confidence for PE selling
If price opens at BB + shows OH → high probability BB Blast fail

concepts/options.title: Options
concepts/options.text:
Options
Definition
A
derivative
contract giving the holder the
right, but not the obligation
, to buy (Call) or sell (Put) an underlying at a fixed
strike price
on/before
expiry
. You pay a
premium
for this right; the premium decays to zero by expiry. Calls carry an up view; Puts carry a down view.
What you actually pay for
Option premium =
Intrinsic Value (chips)
+ Time Value (hawa). See that page for the formulas and the NK house rule:
buy chips (ITM), sell hawa (OTM)
.
Strike classification (relative to current price)
Type
CE
PE
Contains
ATM
strike ≈ spot
strike ≈ spot
mostly hawa
ITM
strike
below
spot
strike
above
spot
chips + hawa (deeper = more chips)
OTM
strike
above
spot
strike
below
spot
only hawa
→ goes to 0 on expiry
⚠️
Critical:
the option price is driven by the
future price
of the underlying, NOT the spot — except on expiry day after 12 noon, when spot takes over.
Key mechanics
Expiry:
index options — weekly (every Thursday) + monthly (last Thursday); stock options — monthly only. If last Thursday is a holiday → previous trading day.
Premium decay:
from purchase to expiry the premium keeps declining toward zero (theta). Weekly OTM ≈
premium / 5
per day (the
18-hour game
).
European-style
in India (NSE symbols end in "E", e.g.
NIFTY 14TH JAN 13000 CE
) — exercisable only on expiry.
Buying vs selling capital:
buying 1 ATM lot = pay the premium (small); selling 1 ATM lot = pay ~future-equivalent margin (large).
Behaviour with
VIX
Higher/rising VIX → rising premium →
good for buyers
.
Lower/falling VIX → falling premium →
good for sellers
.
Never sell options when VIX is high. Never buy OTM when VIX is falling.
Risk framing
Option buyer:
max loss = premium paid; gains can be multifold; capital erodes fast via theta.
Option seller:
max gain = premium; theoretically unlimited risk; needs large margin.
→ This asymmetry is
why
NK hedges: combine buys + sells to cap risk and reduce margin.
Probability of Profit (POP) & Delta as POP Proxy
From
Ravindra Elicherla (EP-73)
: sell options
only when the Probability of Profit (POP) is clearly on your side
— target
≥70-80% POP
via far-OTM strikes. Don't chase premium size; prefer high-probability, small-premium, repeatable trades.
Delta ≈ probability of expiring ITM.
So for a
seller
,
POP ≈ 1 − delta
of the sold option:
Sold option delta
Approx POP (seller)
Read
0.50 (ATM)
~50%
Coin flip — avoid for selling
0.30
~70%
Minimum threshold for income selling

~80%
Ravindra's sweet spot

~90%
Very safe, but tiny premium
This is
why
Rita's
Daily Theta
uses
300 OTM
(≈0.10-0.15 delta → ~85-90% POP) and gets 92.9% WR. The rule is now explicit:
pick strike by target delta, not by premium amount.
Strategy Selection by Regime
Options strategies are
not regime-independent
(except
Arbitrage 2.0
). Before selling premium, classify the regime first — see
Regime Mapping
. Bull put spreads belong in uptrends; in downtrends they become serial losers.
NK's option-buyer discipline (Jul 2026 podcast)
"If you trade every day, you cannot make money by buying options."
5–7 trades/month maximum
for option buyers. "Less trade, best trade." More trades mainly benefit the broker and the government (STT/stamp duty = your "sleeping partner").
The two golden rules
(NK's exact framing):
 1. Intraday →
read volume
(
Nk Volume Reading
).
 2. Swing → follow
Hilega Milega
on
≥ 3-hour TF
.
Don't drop the mindset first:
"I have ₹1L, I want ₹4L/year" — discard this. Treat trading like a business, not a multiple-X target.
Calendar edges for buyers:
April effect:
tax-loss harvesting Mar 20–30 → selling stops →
9 of 10 times market up by Apr 15.
Position for this up-move.

break the option→future→spot chain — work in the buyer's favor.
Provable, not opinion: a low-frequency trader (50% capital, fewer trades) beats a daily trader on year-end ROI. SEBI bars NK from running the contest publicly.

concepts/psychology.title: Psychology And Position Sizing
concepts/psychology.text:
Psychology And Position Sizing
Core Principle
Market can surprise you most when you feel most convinced. Position sizing exists to prevent one emotional or overconfident trade from damaging the account.
Position Sizing Rules
Do not deploy more than 30-40% of capital in one trade.
Exception in source: Hedge 21 may allow 60-80%, but this should be treated as unvalidated and high risk until tested.
For investment, do not deploy more than 5% capital in one stock.
For option buying, do not use more than 10% of total capital.
Keep capital reserved for adjustments.
Investment Allocation Notes
Source suggests 50% in ETFs such as Nifty Bees/N100.
Remaining capital split among group-A sector leaders, mid/small-cap sector leaders, and a small 3-4% high-risk bucket.
Treat as course guidance, not backtested allocation advice.
Behavior Rules
Planned risk before entry.
Do not average losing trades blindly.
Do not increase size after frustration.
Profit preservation matters as much as entry.
Avoid copying trades without understanding the logic.
Backtest Use
Psychology is not directly backtested, but its rules become constraints:
- Max capital per strategy.
- Max loss per trade/day.
- Kill-switch after first planned profit or loss.
- No averaging unless the strategy explicitly defines an adjustment.
NK's exit & mindset discipline (Jul 2026 podcast)
"Exit is everything." Entry is easy; if you can't exit you can't trade. (Abhimanyu analogy — entered the chakravyuha, couldn't exit.)
Book loss in full, immediately. Book profit in two halves.
"Loss ko easy book karo; profit ko easy book mat karo." When in doubt,
cut 50% of the position
— the "heartbeat" warns before danger. Result: long ride when right, short ride when wrong.
"First loss is the smallest loss."
Not booking = you book a bigger loss later. Averaging down a loser turns you into an "accidental investor."
Two exit pains:
booking a loss (obvious), AND booking profit too early then watching it run 100→200 (breeds regret → worse behavior next trade).
Bull markets build false belief
(even donkeys feel skilled);
bear markets steal your belief system.
Retail buys "when the environment is good" = paying the airport/railway-station premium. Buy when the village has nothing (
SRT
< 0.6).
"Gut feeling has zero value in the market."
Be ego-less; admit "I am wrong" first — only then do you start improving.
The "free welfare" trap:
in India only two fields have
everyone
claiming to do you good for free — politics and the stock market. Be deeply suspicious of free market advice; nobody is genuinely trying to make the retailer profitable.
Learn early, unlearn more than you learn.
If you learn wrong things early, unlearning later is extremely painful. Don't learn from people who themselves don't trade profitably.
⚠️ Mindset framing from a podcast — not data. The "cut 50% when in doubt" rule is concrete and usable as a trade-management heuristic.

concepts/regime-mapping.text:
Concept: Regime Mapping
Definition
Regime mapping
is the discipline of
classifying the current market state (regime) BEFORE selecting a strategy
. The strategy follows the regime — never the other way around. From
Ravindra Elicherla (EP-73)
:
"Classify the regime first. The strategy follows the regime."
It is the
top-level filter
that sits above every individual strategy in the system. Without it, a good strategy applied in the wrong regime becomes a losing strategy.
The Four Core Regimes
Regime
Price behavior
Volatility
Best-fit strategies
Uptrend
Higher highs/lows
Expanding then cooling
Bull put spreads, covered calls, cash-secured puts (closer strikes)
Range / Consolidation
Sideways, mean-reverting
Low & stable
Wide credit spreads, covered calls (high delta), Iron Condors
Volatile / Choppy
Whipsaw both directions
High (VIX elevated)
Wider spreads
smaller size
, or stand aside; avoid naked premium
Downtrend
Lower highs/lows
Expanding
Cash-secured puts at
lower
strikes (paid to wait), reduce/stop call-selling, raise cash
The
VIX
level and trend are the fastest regime proxy: low+falling VIX = uptrend/range; rising VIX = transition; high VIX = volatile/downturn risk.
The Rule
No regime = no trade.
If you cannot clearly place the market into one of the four boxes, the default action is
stand aside
. Discipline over activity.
This directly counters the most common retail mistake: forcing a favourite strategy into every market condition.
How to Determine the Regime (checklist)
Index trend
— Nifty above/below its 20 & 50 SMA? (Daily + Weekly)
VIX level & direction
— VIX < 15 and falling = calm; VIX > 20 and rising = stress
Market breadth
— advances vs declines; are leaders or laggards up?
BB structure
—
BB
squeeze (range) vs walk (trend) vs trap (reversal)
Recent failure rate
— if your last 3-4 trades of a type failed, the regime likely shifted against that type

⭐ Regime Filter for Daily Theta (pending backtest)
Ravindra's
framework suggests:
skip Daily Theta credit-spread trades when the regime is "Downtrend"
(Nifty below 50 SMA + VIX rising). This is a candidate lift to the existing 92.9% WR — see backtest queue below.
Why It Matters
A bull put spread is a
high-win-rate strategy in an uptrend
and a
serial loser in a downtrend
. The strategy didn't change — the regime did.
Most strategy "failures" are actually
regime misapplications
. Regime mapping catches this before entry.
It is the single highest-leverage addition to Rita's system: it costs nothing and filters out the worst trades.
Backtest Candidates
Regime-gated Daily Theta
— does skipping credit spreads when Nifty < 50 SMA + VIX rising improve PF beyond 1.77?

Covered-call regime filter
— does disabling covered calls in index downtrends reduce assignment-during-drawdown risk?
Limitations
Regime classification has
lag
— by the time a downtrend is obvious, much of the damage is done. Leading indicators (VIX spike, breadth thrust) help but aren't perfect.
Overlays with
S/R
and
VIX
— not a fully independent signal.
Subjective element: "range" vs "choppy" can be hard to distinguish in real time.

SRT Investing
Definition
SRT is a long-term investing ratio:
SRT = latest spot / 124-day SMA
124 days ≈ 6 months ≈ 50% of ~248 trading days. The source uses it to identify broad Nifty investment zones.
Rules
SRT between 0.6 and 0.9 is considered a strong investing zone.
Monthly HM should be buy before investing.
Add in batches:
30% capital when SRT reaches 0.9.
Add every 0.1 downside.
Safe investment areas also include weekly AVWAP / 20 SMA and convergence of 20, 50, 124, 150, 200 EMA.
NK's refined thresholds (Jul 2026 podcast)
Nifty SRT normally oscillates
0.55 to 1.5

SRT level
Meaning
Action

Lifetime wealth-creation zone
Never short, even if paid to.
Occurs once every 10–14 years (last: Covid 2020; Nifty "Lakshman Rekha" 7410, low 7411)
~0.85
Nifty ~17% off its top
Positional BUY zone — hold ~6 months
Weekly > 1.24
Overheated
Exit equities → gold / dividend-yielding / cash. Even if it runs to 1.30 (+30%), the exit was right
Critical: always check SRT on DAILY, not monthly
— monthly shows ~1.53 and misleads.
Nifty drawdown ladder:
5% → 12% → 17% → 36–38%. A break of 36–38% = crash to 50–58% (as in 2008 / Covid). 17% breaks only on genuinely bad news.
Cross-instrument caveat:
stock/commodity SRT levels differ from Nifty's — do NOT apply Nifty SRT levels to other instruments.

to

for faster response.

Entry ladder at 0.9, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6.
Exit variants: SRT mean reversion, fixed holding period, monthly HM sell.

Price zones where the market has historically paused, reversed, or broken out. Support is a floor where buying pressure tends to emerge. Resistance is a ceiling where selling pressure tends to emerge.

concepts/survivorship-bias.title: Concept: Survivorship Bias (the Wald Lesson)
concepts/survivorship-bias.text:
Concept: Survivorship Bias (the Wald Lesson)
Definition
Survivorship bias
is the logical error of drawing conclusions from only the things that
survived
a process, while ignoring those that did not (because they're invisible). The classic example is the
Abraham Wald WWII aircraft-armor story
.
The Wald Story
During WWII, the Allies examined returning bomber aircraft and plotted bullet-hole locations, planning to add armor where holes were densest. Statistician
Abraham Wald
pointed out the flaw:
the armor should go where there are NO holes.
The planes with holes in those places didn't make it back — they crashed. The returning planes were the
survivors
; the data was missing exactly the failures that mattered most.
The Trading Application
From
Ravindra Elicherla (EP-73)
:
"Study the trades that failed and the accounts that blew up, not just the winners. That's the Wald lesson."
In markets, survivorship bias appears everywhere:
Survivor data (visible)
The missing failures (invisible)
"Top 10 options strategies" lists
Strategies that blew up accounts and were abandoned
Successful trader interviews
The 95% who quit after losing their capital
Stocks currently in Nifty 50
Stocks that were delisted/expelled (their returns drop out of indices)
"I made 50% on this trade" posts
The same trader's losing trades they didn't post
Backtests on today's NSE 500
Companies that went bankrupt/delisted during the backtest period
Why It's Dangerous for Rita's System
Backtest bias:
If a backtest uses
today's
stock list (e.g., current Nifty 500), it omits companies that failed during the period — making returns look better than reality. Rita's
data/nse200_symbols.csv
and
data/nse500_symbols.csv
are
current
lists → potential survivorship bias in every backtest run on them.
Strategy-selection bias:
Reading only about strategies that worked for successful traders hides the ones that looked identical but ruined accounts.
Confirmation bias amplifier:
We remember winning trades and forget losers → overconfidence in a strategy's edge.
How to Counter It
Ask "what's missing from this sample?"
before trusting any return figure.
Track every trade
, wins and losses, in the paper-trade trackers — Rita already does this (CSVs in
papertrades/
). Keep the losers visible.
Use point-in-time universes
for backtests where possible (the stock list as it
was
on each date, not today's). Flag this as a backtest-accuracy improvement.
Study blow-ups explicitly.
Read about strategies/accounts that failed, not just successes.
In the
Arbitrage 2.0
DRREDDY post-mortem
approach: do a write-up on every loss, not just wins.
Specific Risks in Rita's Current Data
data/ohlcv_daily.csv
covers 2024-01 to 2026-07 for
currently listed
stocks.
Stocks delisted during this window are absent
→ any backtest (BB Trap, Open=Low, base-after-decline) over-estimates returns slightly.
The NSE 500 / Smallcap 250 lists fetched today won't include names expelled since 2024.
This is a
known, accepted limitation
— flagged here so it isn't forgotten. Magnitude is usually small over 2.5 years but non-zero.
Mental Model Summary
When you only count the survivors, you learn the wrong lesson.
Armor the places with no bullet holes.
Related Concepts
Psychology
— discipline, overconfidence, loss aversion
Regime Mapping
— survivorship bias distorts regime read if you ignore failed regimes
Hedging
— hedging exists precisely because the "invisible" tail outcomes matter most
Sources

— explicit Wald reference and trading application

concepts/toofani.title: Toofani
concepts/toofani.text:
Toofani
Definition
Toofani is a support/resistance-based weekly options spread. It sells current-expiry premium at an expected expiry zone and buys next-week protection around the same side.
Setup
Mark support and resistance where weekly expiry is likely.
Sell current-expiry PE at support or CE at resistance.
Buy next-week protection with 8-10 points debit or credit.
Treat 1-hour/3-hour close beyond support/resistance as invalidation.
Adjustment
Exit with minor loss, or
Convert into bull spread / bear spread with 2x lot, or
Sell additional PE at resistance / CE at support as described by source.
Backtest Specification
Needs option chain by weekly expiry.
Define support/resistance mechanically before testing.
Test invalidation using 1-hour and 3-hour candle close.
Compare next-week buy debit versus credit variants.

concepts/udd-ja.text:
Udd Ja
Definition
Udd Ja is a bullish intraday cash-stock momentum pattern. It looks for all-timeframe bullish stocks where VWAP/AVWAP become flat, volume dries up, and a breakout triggers a quick move.
Setup
Stock bullish on higher timeframes.
Monthly/weekly BB blast preferred.
VWAP and AVWAP flat on 15-minute chart.
Confirm flat VWAP/AVWAP on 3-minute chart.
Price stays above VWAP.
Volume dries up during 11 AM-1 PM consolidation.
Sudden volume spike and BB breakout starts the move.
Entry And Exit
Entry: breakout close above consolidation high, or pullback during Bollinger walk.
Preferred timing: after 1 PM.
Target: 2-3x morning range, adjusted for move already completed.
SL: one candle close below AVWAP, or one point below VWAP.
Exit when Bollinger walk ends or price returns toward VWAP.
Important Rule
Never sell options during Udd Ja; source says option premium expands and can multiply.
Backtest Specification
Universe: cash stocks with intraday data and volume.
Required indicators: VWAP, AVWAP anchored to 22 Mar 2020 or tested anchor variants, BB.
Signal: flat VWAP/AVWAP + dry volume + consolidation breakout.
Exit variants: 2x range, 3x range, VWAP/AVWAP close, EOD.

VWAP (Volume-Weighted Average Price)
Definition
VWAP = cumulative (price × volume) / cumulative volume — reset daily. It represents the
"fair price"
where the average participant has traded.

"Get on the train near VWAP" — VWAP is the station; price keeps returning to it.

Trend Direction
VWAP curving
up
+ price above VWAP → bullish → every dip to VWAP = buy opportunity
VWAP curving
down

VWAP
flat

Intraday Behavior
Most effective for
intraday
trading (incorporates volume)
After
12:45 PM

VWAP acts as dynamic
S/R

When combined with
Bollinger Bands

Upper/Lower bands = major S/R

Previous day resistance
acts as resistance for the next day only

If price

sources/source-21-candlesticks.text:
21 CANDLESTICKS (Every trader should know)
Original file:
../21_Candlesticks.pdf
(2.4 MB, ~1290 lines extracted — the longest source)
Ingested:
2026-06-23
Summary (2 lines)
A comprehensive Western candlestick-pattern catalogue — single-candle (doji family, hammer, hanging man, marubozu, spinning top, high wave), two-candle (engulfing, harami, piercing, dark cloud, tweezers, kicking), and three/five-candle patterns (morning/evening star, three soldiers/crows, rising/falling three methods, abandoned baby, ladder bottom). This is a
reference encyclopedia
, not NK-specific strategy.
Key takeaways
Single-candle patterns:
-
Doji
= equilibrium, indecision. Variants: long-legged (large upper shadow, weak if close < midpoint), gravestone (rallied then closed at open — ominous at tops), dragonfly (sold off then returned to open — often resolves bullish).
-
Hanging man
(after uptrend) &
Hammer
(after downtrend) — lower shadow ≥ 2× body, tiny/no upper shadow; confirm next day. Color: black body stronger signal than white.
-
Marubozu
= no/short shadows, large body → extreme conviction (white = buyers, black = sellers); watch next day for follow-through.
-
Spinning top
= small body + small shadows + low volume = disinterest.
-
High wave
= small body + very long both shadows = tug-of-war, indecision, possible trend shift.
Two-candle patterns:
-
Bullish/Bearish Engulfing
— 2nd candle's real body fully engulfs the 1st (shadows need not be engulfed).
-
Harami
(bullish/bearish) — small 2nd body inside large 1st body; reversal signal.
-
Piercing
(bullish) /
Dark Cloud Cover
(bearish) — 2nd candle closes > halfway into prior body.
-
Tweezers
(top/bottom) — two sessions share identical/near-identical highs or lows.
-
Kicker
— explosive: gap open above prior high+close (bullish) or below prior low+close (bearish); "shock event."
Three/five-candle patterns:
-
Morning Star / Evening Star
— long body → small star (gap) → long body reversing ≥50% into day-1 body.
-
Three White Soldiers
(bullish, post-decline+consolidation) /
Three Black Crows
(bearish, each close lower).
-
Rising/Falling Three Methods
— continuation: long body + 3 small opposite bodies contained within it + long body resuming.
-
Abandoned Baby
(rare, no confirmation needed) — long black → doji gap-down → long white gap-up.
-
Ladder Bottom, Three Stars in the South, Concealing Baby Swallow, Upside Gap Two Rabbits
— rarer reversals.
-
On Neck / In Neck / Thrusting
— downtrend continuation (each closes slightly higher into prior black body).
-
Side-by-Side White Lines, Homing Pigeon, Matching Low, Deliberation, Advance Block, Mat Hold, J-Hook, Cradle, Scoop, Stick Sandwich, Dumpling Top, Fry Pan Bottom, Tower Top/Bottom, Three Line Strike, Meeting Line, Separating Line, Thrusting Line, 8-10-12-13 new price lines
— all catalogued with recognition criteria.

Source: A-19 Adjustment and Ehlers Fisher
Summary
Class notes on Ehlers Fisher confirmation, ratio-trade placement, OH-OL interpretation, A-19 adjustment, and spread profit booking.
Ehlers Fisher Rules
Use Ehlers Fisher with 21 EMA on 10-minute timeframe for expiry intraday confirmation.
Above 0 line and rising, above VWAP: buy-side bias.
Near +4.5 to +6.8: overbought zone.
Near -4.5 to -6.8: oversold zone.
Exit buy trade when Ehlers Fisher touches or moves below 0.
Bearish view when the indicator is below 0; price is less likely to rise until it comes back above 0.
Ratio Trade Notes
Ratio trades can use deep OTM, deep ITM, ATM, OTM, or far OTM, but the risk zone must be known first.
Best in rangebound markets where the market moves within a broad 1000-1500 point area.
If upside band blast occurs, exit and convert to a bull call spread.
Ratio should be made above resistance, not near support.
A-19 Adjustment
Risk is mainly buying premium minus selling premium, but fast 1500 point moves can create visible losses if not adjusted.
Periodically book profit from the sell side.
If market falls, sell far OTM calls over time; never sell below the buying strike because it can trap the trade.
If market jumps sharply to the next view zone, exit both legs and rebuild the position at the new strike zone.
Buy side exists mainly to protect drastic upside and reduce margin; actual edge is sold premium decay.
Profit Booking
First calculate maximum possible profit.
Book around 40-45% of maximum profit in stock spread trades.
In far OTM stock spreads, exit can be around 60-70%.
In index spreads, exit around 60-70% of maximum profit.

Source: A-19 Double, A100 Expiry, Time Track
Summary
Primary A-19 source. It describes a ratio-style options hedge where one option is bought and two options are sold, plus A100 monthly-expiry futures gap trading and time-track option selling.
A-19 Double
Structure: buy 1 lot, sell 2 lots.
Avoid when VIX is above 23 because large 200-300 point gaps can move outside the expected range.
Also avoid when VIX is falling from a convergence point, because a steady 500-600 point rally can occur.
Nifty example: buy monthly 16000 CE and sell two monthly 16300 CE when spot is near 15821.
Strike logic: buy strike plus buy premium gives the approximate sell strike, rounded to the nearest strike.
Keep buying premium slightly higher than total selling premium; the debit is the defined downside risk.
Weekly far OTM buy can reduce margin and protect against random overnight moves.
Can be built on CE or PE side, and in stocks, Nifty, Bank Nifty, gold, silver, or currency.
Claimed Payoff Behavior
Downside loss is limited to the buy-sell debit.
Rangebound market should be favorable due to sold premium decay.
Upside is protected up to a defined range, but loss begins if expiry moves beyond the upper breakeven.
Extra intraday income can be generated by selling far OTM options only when technical direction supports it.
A100 Expiry Arbitrage
Trades the gap between current-month and next-month futures on monthly expiry day.
If current future has premium over spot and next future has larger premium, sell current future and buy next future.
If current future is below spot, buy current future and short next future.
Entry windows: around 9:30 AM and again near 12:50 PM if the gap recreates.
Use basket orders.
Time Track Selling
Execute around 9:30 AM or 2:30 PM.
Short straddle or strangle on Nifty/Bank Nifty.
Sum-wise SL: total premium received plus about 10 points; exit if sustained for more than 2 minutes.
In stock options after the 15th of the month, short both call and put around 2:30 PM for small daily decay; source mentions Rs 1 SL on a Rs 7 premium example.
Backtest Notes
A-19 needs explicit payoff modeling by strike, premium, expiry, VIX, and adjustment rules.
A100 needs futures EOD/intraday data across expiry days.
Time Track is a separate intraday options-selling strategy; do not mix results with A-19.

Source: Anna Coulling — A Complete Guide to Volume Price Analysis
Source
Book:
A Complete Guide to Volume Price Analysis
Author:
Anna Coulling
Reference:
Scribd document 531334486
Length:

Ingestion note:
Scribd preview returned only the description and topic outline, not the full body text. Page below captures the framework from the published summary. Full re-ingestion requires the PDF.
Summary
Foundational text on
Volume Price Analysis (VPA)
— reading price action and volume together to "think like market insiders." Volume validates price movements and reveals accumulation, distribution, and market manipulation that price alone hides.
Three Core Pillars
1. Price + Volume = Insider View
Combine price action with volume to understand what market insiders (smart money) are doing
Volume validates price moves — price lies, volume doesn't
Reveals
accumulation
(smart money buying quietly) and
distribution
(smart money selling quietly)
Volume exposes
market manipulation
that pure price charts hide
2. Wyckoff's Three Laws
Coulling's VPA is built on Richard Wyckoff's framework:
Law
Meaning
Supply & Demand
Price moves based on imbalance between buyers (demand) and sellers (supply). Volume reveals which side is dominant.
Cause & Effect
Accumulation/distribution phases (the "cause") build energy that determines the size of the subsequent markup/markdown (the "effect"). Longer consolidation = bigger move.
Effort vs Result
Volume = effort; price spread = result. If high volume (effort) produces small price move (result), the move is weak — reversal likely. If low volume produces big move, move is strong.
3. Key Techniques
Volume at Price (VAP):
Volume distribution across price levels (not time) — reveals where real S/R sits
Volume Price Analysis (VPA):
Reading each candle's volume relative to its price spread
Buying/Selling Climaxes:
High-volume exhaustion moves that mark trend ends
Anomaly detection:
Volume spikes that don't match price action = warning signal
Topics Covered (from document outline)
Market manipulation & insider trading
Accumulation & distribution phases

Summary (2 lines)
The definitive BB Trap manual: identification rules, 4 hedged trade variants (cash intraday, future+hedge, call spread, put spread), worked examples on Indigo/BankNifty, AVWAP option-selling rules, and the "Jackpot Trade" variant when all three timeframes align. This is the most complete BB Trap source.
Key takeaways
BB Trap = retailers trapped on a fake gap move.
Price gaps up/down → retailers pile in → smart money sells into them → price collapses back below VWAP. SL: above high of the outside-band candle.
4 ways to trade
(choose by capital, risk, emotion):
 1.
Cash intraday
— sell short, MIS only, never NRML/carry.
 2.
Short Future + sell ATM Put
— directional + premium income. (Example: Indigo future 1672, short 1600 PE @67.95 → net +31 pts.)
 3.
Sell Call above VWAP
— naked or hedged (buy call 50 pts above sold strike). Hedged profit smaller (~8–9 pts) but no system SL needed.
 4.
Buy 1-strike-away OTM Put + sell far OTM Put
— defined risk = buy−sell premium. Example: buy 1660 PE @67 + sell 1620 PE @48 → max risk ₹19 for full month.
Jackpot Trade:
BB Trap on all three TFs (15/30/60 min) simultaneously → very big move, occurs once in 2–3 months. "Very little SL hunting."
Frequency:
5–6 times/month in indices, 2–3 in a stock. Works in intraday only (positional uses daily TF).
Buy Monthly option
to protect against premium loss in intraday.
When NOT to trade:
lower-band BB Trap + Open=High, or upper-band BB Trap + Open=Low → avoid.
BB Trap + Three-Step pattern is supreme
— ignore Hilega-Milega signals when both form together. Retailer trapping doesn't show on indicators until later.
AVWAP section (also in this PDF)
Anchors = where FIIs/DIIs enter. Find 2 fear-point lows on Nifty daily chart → set as anchors.
Option selling with AVWAP:
enter near anchor, SL = anchor itself. If price closes above anchor → SL hit; below → stay in trade.
Rule:
above anchor → buy option; below anchor → sell option. If both CE and PE under anchor → both go to 0.
Works across all instruments: stocks, futures, options, commodities, currencies.
Option chart: plot AVWAP from 4–5 months before the option's birth.

Mentorship 3 — BB Trap Chart Reading + Hedging (7 Feb 2020)
Original file:

(2.4 MB, ~223 lines extracted)
Ingested:

Summary (2 lines)
The early mentorship session that first codifies BB Trap rules and hedging methods. Adds the RSI-50 filter, the "midline breaker" BB usage for choppy markets, and detailed hedge math (ITM vs ATM vs OTM vs OTM hedging). More raw/teaching-style than the later BB Trap PDF.
Key takeaways
Price follows the higher time frame.
Always follow 1-hour TF; use 30-min for entry.
RSI rule (hourly):
never sell until RSI < 50 (the "blue, water" level); never buy until RSI > 50.
20 SMA as SL/exit:
stay in trade as long as 20 SMA isn't breached and 50 RSI doesn't cross. Above 20 SMA = buy zone; below = sell zone.
Midline breaker:
when 20 SMA gets breached repeatedly (choppy), use Bollinger Bands instead — upper = resistance, lower = support. BB blast on hourly after consolidation = "big money" trade; naked option OK here.
BB Trap rules (formalized here):
1. 15-min / 30-min / 1-hour TF.
 2. Good gap up/down open only.
 3. Min 1 candle closed outside the band.
 4. Next candle inside band AND closes below low of outside-band candle.
 5. Following candles stay below VWAP and sustain → then short.
 6. Pattern stays for the full day. Take ATM options.
Hedge methods for BB Trap:
ITM vs ATM:
buy ITM (70%+ chips) + sell ATM. When premium is high; used intraday; expects smaller movement. Risk = buying − selling. Even if market stays flat → profitable.
OTM vs OTM:
buy 1-strike OTM + sell further OTM. When chart reading says big move is coming. Max risk = small debit. Example (SBI): buy 370 PE @9.10 + sell 360 PE @6.70 → max risk ₹2.40 for the month; profit if SBI drops even to 380 from 398.
Future hedge:
short future + short ATM put (high VIX) or buy call (low VIX).
Option hedge rule of thumb:
if buying call, sell 2 strikes above; if buying put, sell 2 strikes below. Or: sell ATM when taking future.
Lower BB = support, upper BB = resistance
— price may turn from either band.

Price repeatedly rejected at 20 SMA, then bounces off 200 SMA → usually breaks 20 SMA upward.

intraday-only; above = buy, below = sell;
don't trade VWAP alone

use

sellers

For option
buyers

Exit/SL:
exit is more important than entry. 20 SMA on day TF = exit zone; usually broken only via gap up/down or a big candle (no chance to run). Static S/R also good exit. "20 SMA opposite side = best entry."
Trading rule:
market near resistance → focus on top losers; near support → focus on top gainers.
Overbought/oversold:
Overbought = stock over-held by retailers; oversold = big money (FIIs/DIIs/punters) selling.
A crashed stock with too many retailers won't rise until retailers exit.
HM > 86 on monthly

Oversold entry: when HM RSI hits 15 and goes flat, then starts to curve → take the trade.

Uptrend + middle BB line rising → buy; bring to 20 SMA on smaller TF + buy signal → buy.
Market stuck in one place + BB narrow +
BB blast
→ big move likely. But if BB was
not
narrow and it blasts → likely a
trap
.
Day-TF BB event → 7–28 days effect; hourly → 2–3 days effect.
Confirmation: BB blast + next day gap up + sustain = confirmed blast.
Moh-Maya:
big news + day-TF doji-type candle outside the band → next day when 1-hr closes above VWAP → take the trade. Safe version: buy monthly expiry option of ₹60–100 near close; book 50% on double, 25% at 20 SMA, else hedge; SL below doji close.
